title: PAR-07/S8 duplicate DataIndex target generated fast slice
scope: Audit duplicate DataStorage DataIndex target handling against ODA v5.4.1 §24.2.2.2–.3
Lock duplicate-target diagnostics and replay refusal for exact and schema-index-variant rows with generated in-memory bytes
Reuse the existing AC1027 DataIndex-order fast test and CTest

method.specificationAuthority: ODA Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1 §24.2.2.2–.3

sources.project: ODA Open Design Specification for .dwg files v5.4.1
sources.observed: DataIndex rows contain segment index, local offset, and schema index; the data-record algorithm uses each row's local offset to locate a record header containing the object handle and data-local offset.
sources.limits: The cited text does not explicitly state that duplicate (segmentIndex, localOffset) tuples are prohibited for every producer. The test records the local conservative ambiguity/replay-safety policy, not a universal normative validity conclusion.

sources.observed: readDataIndex already emits datastorage-duplicate-data-index-entry and omits a repeated (segmentIndex, localOffset) target tuple, regardless of schemaIndex; its structural diagnostic disables replay. The existing AC1027 generated DataIndex-order test lacked dedicated assertions for exact and schema-index-variant duplicate targets.
sources.limits: This slice adds regression coverage only; it does not change production handling, peer qualification, geometry semantics, or the overall support boundary.

decision.planDelta: Added source/spec boundary analysis and generated negative controls for exact duplicate DataIndex tuples and the same physical target with a different schemaIndex. Both assert duplicate-target diagnosis, one omitted index/record, structural invalidity, and replay refusal. The normative gap is documented explicitly: ODA's cited text explains target resolution but does not expressly declare duplicate pairs universally invalid.

validation.commitBlocker: No commit attempted; the shared worktree contains extensive unrelated user changes and Git metadata is read-only in this environment.
